title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — May 21, 2026
summary: A University of Copenhagen study published May 21 in Science Advances identified a new thermal kill mechanism in corals: warming oceans collapse microscopic surface cilia before visible bleaching occurs, suggesting corals are more vulnerable than current monitoring captures. The Ocean Cleanup and Kia announced May 15 expansion of Interceptor technology to the Los Angeles River and San Gabriel River ahead of the LA28 Olympics, as part of the 30 Cities Program. Two new map points were added for the LA cleanup sites. Nearly 200 conservation groups formally urged Congress on May 13 to reject H.R. 8509, which would delay ropeless fishing gear requirements until 2035 and threatens the ~380 remaining North Atlantic right whales. The Melanesian Ocean Summit adopted the MOCOR Declaration for regional Pacific ocean protection at Port Moresby on May 15.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — Fri May 15, 2026
summary: Kia and The Ocean Cleanup Expand Interceptor Network to Los Angeles and San Gabriel Rivers Ahead of LA28 Olympics. Melanesian Ocean Summit Adopts MOCOR Declaration for Regional Pacific Ocean Protection.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — May 13, 2026
summary: Norway froze its UNEP funding in May 2026, threatening secretariat support for the stalled global plastics treaty negotiations ahead of the still-unscheduled INC-5.4. Conservation groups filed a legal motion to defend NOAA's right whale vessel speed rules after the Trump administration backed legislation to delay new rope regulations until 2035. The 2025–26 North Atlantic Right Whale calving season was confirmed closed with 23 calves — the highest count since 2009. Heat-resistant 'super corals' capable of surviving 36°C are showing promise in scaled reef restoration, and Canon and Oceans Alive Foundation launched a coral rehabilitation initiative along Kenya's northern coastline.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — May 06, 2026
summary: The 2025–2026 North Atlantic Right Whale calving season closed with 23 confirmed calves — the highest count since 2009 — but the Trump administration's backing of H.R. 8509 to delay new fishing regulations until 2035 threatens to erase the conservation gains. The Ocean Cleanup crossed 50 million kg of plastic removed in March 2026 and deployed its first river Interceptor in the Philippines (Meycauayan River, projected 370–540 tonnes/year). A new peer-reviewed study warned that 70% of Caribbean coral reefs have already shifted from growth to net erosion due to the 2023–24 marine heatwave — years ahead of climate model predictions. California held public hearings on the proposed Mishopshno State Marine Conservation Area, which would become the first tribally led MPA in state history.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — Apr 29, 2026
summary: The BBNJ High Seas Treaty has climbed to 92 ratifications as of late April 2026, up from 81 at entry into force in January, with PrepCom 3 (concluded April 2) advancing CoP1 planning for January 2027. Earth Day 2026 celebrated the historic crossing of 10% global ocean protection and the WTO Fisheries Subsidies Agreement entering into force. North Atlantic Right Whale Day (April 23) brought cautious optimism with 22-23 calves spotted in the 2025-2026 season — an encouraging increase after years of low birth rates. The global plastics treaty elected a new INC chair at INC-5.3 in February 2026, with substantive negotiations on production caps scheduled to resume at INC-5.4 later this year.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — Wed Apr 22, 2026

The MSC Foundation marked the first anniversary of its Marine Conservation Center at Ocean Cay, MSC Marine Reserve in the Bahamas on Earth Day, April 22, 2026.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — Apr 21, 2026
summary: The Ocean Cleanup has now removed 45 million kg of plastic from oceans and rivers — a tenfold increase since January 2024 — with 2025 the most productive year on record at 25 million kg. The IUCN formally upgraded the North Atlantic Right Whale to Critically Endangered this month with ~400 individuals remaining, while a U.S. federal court ruled the American lobster industry violates the Endangered Species Act. Global ocean protection crossed 10.01% for the first time, Ghana designated its first-ever Marine Protected Area, and UK researchers unveiled AI system BlueBiome to improve coral restoration success rates. The BBNJ High Seas Treaty, now in force since January 17, 2026, saw its third and final PrepCom session conclude with implementation progress but a critical gap on subsidiary body nominations that could delay the first high-seas MPAs.

title: Ocean Cleanup Tracker Update — Tue Apr 14, 2026
summary: Ghana officially declared its first Marine Protected Area on April 14, 2026, following more than 15 years of advocacy by fishing communities, scientists, and NGOs. UK researchers unveiled BlueBiome on April 14, 2026 — an AI-driven system designed to assess coral health and detect bleaching thermal stress earlier than conventional monitoring.
